subject: Accepted: SICK // Encord Data Curation
Re: Measuring labelling team performance
text:
Hey Winnie,

Great question! On-brand evaluation is just one type of evaluation we do,
so this answer will be more generalized.

   - We structure labelling and evaluation per project, with each project
   tied to a specific AI feature and goal (e.g. Image to Design: how well a
   model reconstructs a design based on an image; Design Generation: how well
   a model generates a design based on a prompt
      - With that, we create specific guidelines and determine dimensions
      depending on what we want to evaluate
   - Guidelines are designed to be explicit and operationalised:
      - step-by-step annotation instructions or decision-tree/checklist
      style evaluation workflows
      - clear definitions of core principles, edge cases, and failure modes
      - written under the assumption that labellers have no prior Canva or
      design knowledge, so different backgrounds still converge on the same
      decisions
      - with real-world examples based on model outputs
   - This approach reduces subjectivity and grey areas and encourages
   labellers not to rely on individual taste or preference
      - However, we do have some tasks that measure user preferences so
      that's a different story!
   - During labelling, the labellers are encouraged to ask questions and
   flag ambiguities, especially as new or tricky cases emerge
   - After the evaluation (or sometimes even as the evaluation is
   happening), we run quality assurance loops appropriate to the task, such as
   spot checks, peer review, or formal alignment-rate measurements
   - Finally, guidelines are treated as living documents and are iterated
   based on labeller feedback, recurring FAQs, and QA findings to continuously
   improve consistency and alignment over time

Hope this helps, let me know if you have follow-ups 🫡

Best,
Vida

text:
Hi Moritz,

Here are our questions and feedback on the order form.
1. We would like to check the termination conditions, especially in case
that we would like to terminate the contract for any reason.

have on the terms
3. Platform users should be 3 for now.

25% more than what we currently spend. Please suggest any discount
maintaining the head counts.
5. you are charging with hourly price. I wonder how you would report the
measurement of hourly work. It would be great if you share how you manage
hourly task and how you would report to us in the meeting time.

We are searching for a company that can do video annotation as well as
provide a nicer platform with the similar expense. We are reluctant to jump
in a yearly contract with higher expense and uncertain throughput and
quality unless there is any favorable price and termination conditions. We
can discuss this in the meeting tomorrow.
Thank you.

Daniel
